items.name: theme-deckard
items.title: Deckard theme
items.description: The default deck look. Quiet off-white paper in light mode, a blue-black sheet in dark mode, one teal accent on eyebrows, buttons, and focus rings. Content sits on near-opaque cards with a hairline border and a soft shadow, corners at 1rem. Backgrounds are soft: a top wash, a 44px grid, or a wide spotlight, each with a blurred corner glow. Use it when you want a deck that reads as a modern product presentation and you do not want to design a theme. It defines the full slide token contract from @deckard/core/styles.css (--slide-font-*, the seven size tokens, --slide-padding-*, --slide-radius*, --slide-surface*, and the background colors) plus the shadcn color tokens, all scoped to .deckard-theme on the slide canvas so the app chrome around the deck keeps its own theme. Supports light and dark. Installs into deck/theme/ as three files you own and edit; THEME.md explains which token does what.
items.docs: The theme lands in deck/theme/. Point your deck at it with `import { theme } from "@/deck/theme"` and pass it to `defineDeck({ theme })`. Read deck/theme/THEME.md before changing tokens. Installing another Deckard theme overwrites these three files, because a deck has exactly one theme.

items.name: theme-broadsheet
items.title: Broadsheet theme
items.description: An editorial print look. Warm newsprint in light mode, warm ink in dark mode, oxblood accent in light and terracotta in dark. Everything is serif, from a system stack that loads no web font, and everything is flat: --slide-radius is 0.125rem and --slide-surface-shadow is none, so a content card is a panel with a hairline rule instead of a floating object. Backgrounds are print furniture: horizontal ruled lines for the grid variant, two vertical column rules at the thirds for spotlight. Type runs one step larger at the top of the scale and one step smaller at the bottom than the default theme, and headings carry -0.015em tracking. Use it for a talk that should read as a written argument rather than a product demo, or as a worked example of a second theme built on the same token contract. Defines the same tokens as theme-deckard, scoped to .broadsheet-theme. Supports light and dark. Installs into deck/theme/ as three files you own and edit.

items.name: theme-ledger
items.title: Ledger theme
items.description: A bound report. Warm paper in light mode, warm ink in dark, oxblood accent turning rust after dark. Three families do three jobs: serif headings from a system stack, system sans body copy, mono for eyebrows and folio numbers. Every corner is 0rem and --slide-surface-shadow is none, so rules carry the structure and --slide-surface-border sits three steps darker than --border to pay for it. The grid variant is ledger paper, horizontal rules with one accent margin rule down the left; default and spotlight both close on a heavy folio rule set to the content measure. The scale drops hard from 5rem titles to 3.25rem headings, the way a chapter opener sits over the slide it introduces. Reach for it when the deck is a written argument with numbers in it and you want the slides to read as pages. Defines the same token contract as theme-deckard plus --slide-rule and --slide-margin-rule, scoped to .ledger-theme. Supports light and dark. Installs into deck/theme/ as three files you own and edit.

items.name: theme-meridian
items.title: Meridian theme
items.description: The quietest theme in the registry, and that is the whole brief. A near-white blue-gray sheet in light mode, a cool near-black in dark, one mid blue accent used once per slide. One system sans for everything. Cards are flat with a hairline border and 0.625rem corners; --slide-surface-shadow is none in both modes, so the border carries the separation the way the source design draws it. Headings carry -0.03em of tracking, which is the single most identifiable thing about the theme. The type scale is a step under the default theme at every size, because with no decoration the type is the only hierarchy. Backgrounds are half the alpha of every other theme here: one head wash, a drafting grid that fades out behind the copy, one wide radial. Reach for it for a product or planning review where the content should be the loudest thing on the slide. Supports light and dark. Installs into deck/theme/ as three files you own and edit.

items.name: theme-nexus
items.title: Nexus theme
items.description: A flight console. Dark is the home mode and defaultColorMode is pinned to dark, so a deck opens on the blue-black sheet; the light mode is complete and reads as the printed version of the same document. Every heading is uppercase with a hair of positive tracking, and h1 and h2 carry an amber --slide-halo text shadow that goes to none on paper. Surfaces are flat panels with a 0.125rem blueprint corner. The grid variant is the reason to pick it: a 1.75rem cell grid with every fifth line drawn heavier through --slide-grid-major, faded out behind the copy. Spotlight is an approach light off the top edge with a tube vignette under it. The light accent runs a step darker than the source design so an eyebrow clears 4.5:1 on paper. Reach for it for an engineering or systems talk that wants instrument-panel authority. Supports light and dark, dark by default. Installs into deck/theme/ as three files you own and edit.

items.name: theme-phosphor
items.title: Phosphor theme
items.description: A green CRT. Dark is the home mode and defaultColorMode is pinned to dark; light mode turns the tube off and gives you dark green ink on a pale green sheet for handouts and print. One monospace family sets every word on the slide, headings included, uppercase at weight 700. Scanlines are the first background layer of default, grid, and spotlight rather than an overlay, so only background none escapes them, and --slide-scanline is none in light mode. Display headings carry a phosphor bloom through --slide-halo. The grid variant draws a character cell, --slide-cell wide by --slide-grid-size tall; spotlight is the tube, bloom at the centre and falloff into every corner. Every corner is square. The type scale is the smallest here on purpose, since monospace runs about 20 percent wider than a proportional sans. Reach for it for a developer talk, a build report, or anything that should look like it is running rather than presented. Supports light and dark, dark by default. Installs into deck/theme/ as three files you own and edit.

items.name: block-typography
items.title: Slide typography
items.description: Two primitives every other block builds on. Eyebrow is an uppercase accent label at --slide-label-size with --slide-label-tracking letter spacing, in --primary. SlideHeading is an h1 at --slide-heading-size capped at max-w-5xl with an optional lead paragraph at --slide-lead-size in --muted-foreground. Both read the theme's size tokens rather than Tailwind text sizes, so they resize when you retune the type scale. Add this if you are writing your own slide layouts and want the deck's heading rhythm without copying class strings. Every other Deckard block depends on it.

items.name: block-slide-layouts
items.title: Slide layouts
items.description: The four whole-slide frames a deck reaches for most. HeroSlide centers a big --slide-title-size headline with an eyebrow and a lead, for an opener. BreakerSlide is the same type at the same size but left-aligned and vertically centered, for a section divider. ContentSlideCard puts an eyebrow, heading, and lead above a bordered --slide-surface panel that holds the slide body. OpenContentSlide is the same intro with no panel, for content that brings its own frame such as a chart or a table. All four pull the title from useSlideTitle() when you do not pass one, so a slide's title stays defined in one place. They respect --slide-content-gap, --slide-radius-lg, --slide-surface, --slide-surface-border, and --slide-surface-shadow, which means a theme swap restyles them with no edits.

items.name: block-collections
items.title: Slide collections
items.description: Two ways to put a list on a slide without it turning into a wall of bullets. BulletList numbers each item 01, 02, 03 in a left rail and rules the rows off with a bottom border, at --slide-body-size. FeatureGrid lays three cards across on --slide-surface-muted, each with a title and a supporting paragraph at --slide-support-size. Both are presentational and take plain arrays, so a server component can await the data and pass it straight in. Use BulletList for four to six sequential points and FeatureGrid for three parallel ones. Neither scrolls, so trim the copy instead of adding a seventh item.

items.name: block-media
items.title: Slide media
items.description: Photo and video slides that fill the 1920x1080 canvas properly. FullscreenMediaSlide bleeds an image or a video to every edge and lays optional copy over the bottom on one of three scrims, from --slide-media-overlay-subtle to -strong; the framed variant insets it in a bordered surface instead. ImageShowcaseSlide splits the canvas 1.2fr to 0.8fr, image left and a caption panel right. Both take next/image sources, forward blurDataURL from a static import when the source carries one, take unoptimized so an SVG served from public/ skips the image optimizer instead of needing dangerouslyAllowSVG, and use SlideMediaVideo from @deckard/core so video pauses on slides the audience is not looking at. Both pad against --slide-chrome-top and --slide-chrome-bottom, so the deck header and slide counter never sit on top of a caption. Use these instead of dropping an img on a slide, which will not fit the canvas and will not respect the chrome.

items.name: block-metrics
items.title: Slide metrics
items.description: One export, StatGrid, for the three-figures slide every deck reaches for once. It takes exactly three stats, typed as a tuple so a fourth is a compile error, and marks them up as a description list. Each column is a figure at --slide-title-size in --slide-font-heading with an optional unit at --slide-subheading-size, a caption at --slide-support-size capped to 24 characters a line, and a 2px rule across the top in --slide-surface-border. It sets no color of its own, so the rule picks up the theme border weight. A figure is not a heading element, so it carries data-stat-value for themes that treat headings as more than a font: nexus and ledger style it, the other four leave the figure as the block sets it. Take the caption seriously. A number on a slide without the thing it is measured against is decoration, and the 24ch measure is sized for "up from 2.6k", not for a sentence.

items.name: preset-deckard
items.title: Deckard preset
items.description: Everything a new deck needs in one add: the Deckard theme and all five block families. Use this once, right after installing @deckard/core, then write slides. It also adds the one stylesheet line a consumer cannot guess, the @import of @deckard/core/styles.css, which carries the slide token contract and registers the package's own Tailwind source so the runtime classes survive tree shaking. Nothing else has to be wired: @deckard/core ships compiled, so next.config stays empty.
items.docs: The theme lands in deck/theme/ and the blocks in app/slides/blocks/, and the stylesheet import above is the whole build wiring. @deckard/core ships compiled output and its stylesheet registers its own Tailwind source, so there is no transpilePackages entry and no @source line for you to add. What is left is deck code: create deck/deck.ts, pass the installed theme to defineDeck, then render the deck from app/slides/[id]/page.tsx with createSlideRoute from @deckard/core/next.
